decisive_pair.contrast: C009 has more comprehensive support from the clinical record, including the patient's history of HIV and recent symptoms.

response.rationale: C009 is the most likely diagnosis due to the patient's history of HIV, recent symptoms of low-grade fever, and sudden appearance of skin lesions, which are all consistent with an acute HIV syndrome. relations.justification_span: Two days after the initial skin manifestations, he developed fever up to 39°C, chest pain without irradiation, and shortness of breath
The patient presented with low-grade fever (37.5°) and sudden appearance of skin lesions at the base of his penis. He reported recent sexual activity with multiple male partners
Initial examination revealed vesicular and umbilicated lesions on genitals and small lymphadenomegaly in the groin area. No oropharyngeal lesions were detected
Upon admission for chest symptoms, the patient was hemodynamically stable with continuous anterior chest pain exacerbated by deep breathing
